template.name: Classic & Timeless
template.audience: Established congregations with history, a building people love and a multi-generational family
template.summary: A heritage look that still feels current: parchment grounds, deep forest green, brass hairlines and a small burgundy accent, set in Newsreader with a flared humanist sans for reading. Photos sit in ivory mats or inside an arched chapel window.

church.name: Calder Hill Chapel
church.nameCheck: Web search on 2026-11-19 for "Calder Hill Chapel" Richmond Virginia found no church by that name.
church.addressNote: Calder Hill Road is a made-up street.

sundayTimes.style: Hymns, organ and a quiet start

church.pastorsNote: Lead pastors, a married couple, first names only. Samuel preaches most Sundays; Ruth leads care and prayer.
church.missionLine: To know Christ, to love Richmond, and to keep the door open for whoever comes next.
church.announcement: The bell tower is being restored. Help us ring it again by Easter.

palette.name: Burgundy

palette.name: Stone
palette.carriesText: used as text on Parchment and Vellum

contrastMethod: WCAG 2.x relative luminance formula, recomputed with a Node script during the design review on 2026-11-19; every body text pair is at least 4.5:1. Hover panel check: Sage Grey on Moss 4.98:1, Ivory on Moss 8.01:1.

display.use: Headlines, labels in small capitals, quotes, the wordmark

body.axes: FLAR (flare) set to 100 for flared, chiselled stroke endings

shapes.radius: 2px on buttons, fields and tags; square photos and cards; full semicircle for the arch
shapes.rules: Fine double rules (two 1px lines with a 1px gap) under the header, on outline buttons, above pull quotes and before labels; single 1px hairlines between rows
shapes.ornament: One small fleuron (diamond between curls) used at most twice a page: mission section and footer
shapes.arch: A round-topped chapel window frames the hero photo, story posts and the logo mark, always with a brass double outline and a sill line
shapes.buttons: Primary filled (forest on paper, brass light on forest); outline buttons wear the 3px double rule; paired buttons share one width

motion.character: Slow and settled, like turning a heavy page. Nothing bounces; everything eases in and stays.
motion.reveal: Sections rise 22px and fade in as they enter view. JS adds reveal-init only after the observer is ready; reveal-in shows them.
motion.stepColumns: The four numbered columns rise one by one (0.14s apart); a brass rule draws across each, then settles to a short mark. On hover a moss panel wipes up, the title turns italic and the numeral steps forward.
motion.cards: The three photo cards rise in sequence; on hover the print lifts 4px, the photo eases in 4 percent and the title turns burgundy italic.
motion.primaryButtons: A soft ivory sheen crosses once when the button first comes into view and again on hover.
motion.heroWord: doors, table, arms: each word leaves upward before the next rises in, so two words never overlap.
motion.heroPhoto: A 30 second slow zoom inside the arch, alternating.
motion.announcement: The burgundy play button sends out one gentle ring every 2.6 seconds.
motion.statementBand: The chapel interior drifts slightly slower than the page.
motion.photoStrip: Mounted prints drift left in a 70 second loop and pause on hover or focus.
motion.reviews: Cross-fade every 6.2 seconds, paused on hover and focus.
motion.reducedMotion: All animation and transitions stop; the strip becomes a plain horizontal scroller; nothing starts hidden.

photoTreatment.grade: Warm, natural color with a slight warm lift in the shadows; no filters, no black and white, no cool blue grades
photoTreatment.framing: Ivory mats (8 to 10px) with a hairline border and an italic caption, like prints in a family album; the hero sits inside the arch
photoTreatment.subjects: Adults of every age, groups over portraits, real moments: greeting, singing, praying, eating together
photoTreatment.retouching: Overhead wires removed from the sky and the portico columns of the hero exterior; the baptism photo warmed to match the set and the printed graphic on the shirt removed. The concert-lit choir photo was replaced with a warm pews-and-windows photo so the set follows its own photo rules.

logo.concept: An arched chapel door drawn with two lines (the same double rule used across the site), a cross in burgundy or brass standing on a small filled hill: Calder Hill.
lockups: Primary wordmark: mark left, Calder Hill in Newsreader 500, CHAPEL · EST. 1891 in spaced capitals below
Stacked: mark above, name centered, brass double rule, CHAPEL · RICHMOND
Seal: circular text CALDER HILL CHAPEL · RICHMOND · 1891 around the mark
Small mark: forest square with ivory arch and brass cross, for avatars and favicons
logo.clearSpace: The width of the arch on every side
logo.minimumSize: Wordmark 140px wide on screen; mark alone 16px
